name: JailbreakBench
description: An open robustness benchmark for evaluating jailbreak attacks and defenses against LLMs, providing a curated set of harmful behaviors, standardized attack/defense interfaces, and a living leaderboard. Enables reproducible comparison of red-teaming methods by standardizing evaluation protocols that were previously inconsistent across papers. Contains 100 misuse behaviors across ten hazard categories.
evaluation_method: Attack Success Rate (ASR) — fraction of behaviors successfully elicited; judged by LLM-based classifier
typical_sota_score: 5–80% ASR depending on attack method and model (weaker defenses show higher ASR)
reputation: Published at NeurIPS 2024; standard reference for jailbreak research; widely cited in safety and red-teaming literature; living leaderboard updated as new attacks emerge; from UPenn/ETH/EPFL team
notes: NeurIPS 2024. Complements HarmBench with a living repository of adversarial prompts and standardized evaluation code. 100 misuse behaviors across 10 categories (e.g., cybercrime, CBRN, disinformation). Provides jb-bench Python package for reproducible evaluation. Living leaderboard updated as new attack methods are discovered. From a team across UPenn, ETH Zurich, and EPFL.
